policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory field `placed` as updated at this step. Rule 1 (holding): The scene at this decision step is the LAST listed observed step; check that frame first, before any earlier execution frame. If any object line in that last frame ends in 'is held in the gripper', or the fingers there are partly closed (about 46% or less open), choose B: put it into the bin, before any other rule is considered. This holds whatever `placed` contains and however many cubes lie on the table. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. `placed` here is the value as updated at this step: a step whose execution frames show a cube held and whose last frame shows the fingers about 100% open with nothing held counts that cube as placed, so choose C when every goal count is then met, even if cubes of the goal colors remain on the table, including one that reappeared near the bin after the release. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Color choice: a color whose count in the updated `placed` meets its requirement is finished and is never picked again, even if cubes of that color remain visible on the table. If the last entry of `placed` is a color that is still short, pick that color again (one color is finished before the other is started). Otherwise, including when `placed` is empty, take the first color in the goal instruction's order whose count in `placed` is still below its requirement. Point at that cube's center as shown in the scene at this decision step. A candidate is a cube of the needed color reported as a table cube (not held) in the scene at this decision step and at nearly the same place (within about 6 px) in all but at most one of the execution frames of this step; a real cube may be missing from one frame while the arm passes over it (at step #1, with no execution frames, any cube of that color in the scene is a candidate). A detection that first appears during the step, that sits where the held cube was last reported, that is reported within about 35 px of the bin's center (a detection about 30 px from the bin is a bin echo, not a cube), or whose position moves between frames is not a candidate while any stable one exists. Among several stable candidates, prefer the one nearest the bin's reported center without overlapping it; when two candidates are within about 5 px of the same distance to the bin, prefer the one with the larger y (farther forward). The point is that candidate's center as reported in the last frame; a point within about 3 px of that center is correct. Cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is empty, so pick up a cube of a needed color. If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the stable cube of a needed color nearest the bin (not overlapping it), and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube not overlapping the bin. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

fields.name: placed
fields.description: Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. Write the literal [] as this step's value only at the very first decision step, where the carried-in memory is blank and there are no execution steps at all. A carried-in [] that comes with execution steps is a list like any other and is appended to by the check below, so the step after the first placement writes a one-entry list such as ["blue"]. The value is always a JSON array of double-quoted strings, exactly like the carried-in value and the example: ["green", "green"], never ['green', 'green'] and never a blank. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except after a two-part check applied in order: first, does any execution frame of this step contain an object line ending 'is held in the gripper'; second, does the scene at this decision step (the last listed frame) show the fingers about 100% open with no held line. If both hold, the oracle completed the put-into-bin subgoal: append that held cube's color exactly once. The gripper's position when the fingers opened is irrelevant (it is often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center); fingers opening only to 67-99% in an intermediate frame are irrelevant; same-color detections that appear, shift a few px, or vanish on the table in those frames are irrelevant (detections near the opaque bin are echoes of the held cube or bin contents, not table cubes). None of these is a reason to skip the append. e.g. carried-in ["red"] becomes ["red", "red"]; carried-in ["blue", "blue"] after a held-then-released blue cube becomes ["blue", "blue", "blue"]. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. Emit the value character-for-character as a JSON array with double-quoted strings, identical in form to the carried-in value; a single-quoted list such as ['red', 'green'] is a wrong value. e.g. ["green", "green"]
